dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: I've read your résumé, Nam. It's very good, but there are a few grammar mistakes.
dialogue.reading: aɪv ˈrɛd jʊr ˈrɛzəmeɪ, ˈnɑːm. ɪts ˈvɛri ˈɡʊd, bʌt ðɛr ər ə ˈfjuː ˈɡræmər mɪˈsteɪks.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Here you wrote, "I have worked at a supermarket last year."
dialogue.reading: ˈhɪr juː ˈroʊt, aɪ hæv ˈwɜːrkt ət ə ˈsuːpərmɑːrkɪt ˈlæst ˈjɪr.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Yes. With "last year," use the past simple: "I worked at a supermarket last year."
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs. wɪð ˈlæst ˈjɪr, ˈjuːz ðə ˈpæst ˈsɪmpəl: aɪ ˈwɜːrkt ət ə ˈsuːpərmɑːrkɪt ˈlæst ˈjɪr.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: I see. But I still work at the restaurant, so I wrote, "I have worked there since my first year."
dialogue.reading: aɪ ˈsiː. bʌt aɪ ˈstɪl ˈwɜːrk ət ðə ˈrɛstərɑːnt, soʊ aɪ ˈroʊt, aɪ hæv ˈwɜːrkt ðɛr sɪns maɪ ˈfɜːrst ˈjɪr.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: That's right, because you still work there. Now, who are your references?
dialogue.reading: ðæts ˈraɪt, bɪˈkɔːz juː ˈstɪl ˈwɜːrk ˈðɛr. ˈnaʊ, ˈhuː ər jʊr ˈrɛfərənsɪz?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: My manager at the restaurant and Mr. Davis from my internship.
dialogue.reading: maɪ ˈmænɪdʒər ət ðə ˈrɛstərɑːnt ənd ˈmɪstər ˈdeɪvɪs frəm maɪ ˈɪntɜːrnʃɪp.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Yes, I asked them last week. My manager says I'm her best employee!
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs, aɪ ˈæskt ðɛm ˈlæst ˈwiːk. maɪ ˈmænɪdʒər ˈsɛz aɪm hɜːr ˈbɛst ɪmˈplɔɪiː!

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Great. Employers often call references, so that will help. Have you written your cover letter yet?
dialogue.reading: ˈɡreɪt. ɪmˈplɔɪərz ˈɔːfən ˈkɔːl ˈrɛfərənsɪz, soʊ ðæt wɪl ˈhɛlp. hæv juː ˈrɪtən jʊr ˈkʌvər ˌlɛtər ˈjɛt?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Yes, I finished it last night. Could you read it, too?
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs, aɪ ˈfɪnɪʃt ɪt ˈlæst ˈnaɪt. kʊd juː ˈriːd ɪt, ˈtuː?
